specNotes: Protocol validity is based on cited fields, not on current Core output. Optional-field warnings do not make this pair invalid.

IAB Native 1.2 §7.4 Data Asset Types: type 3 = rating, type 6 = price. Neither Core validation, crosscheck.js nor renderNativeToHtml compares the data asset's `type` field against what was requested (crosscheck map §8 item 8) — a returned value of the right kind (data) and length passes regardless of which data type id it claims; this base pair is valid either way and asserts no finding tied to `type`.

IAB Native 1.2 §4.1/§5.1: request-side `privacy` (integer) and `eventtrackers` (array of {event, methods[]}); response-side `privacy` (string URL) and `eventtrackers` (array of {event, method, url}). Neither field is read anywhere in packages/core (schema, crosscheck) nor in the Inspector's native renderer — they are spec-legal, inert payload for this corpus and require no dedicated finding.
Browser assertions are proposed observables; this corpus has not been run in a browser for this case.
Do not infer rendering from analysis.status or iframe existence alone.

HTTPS Native image URLs use reserved .test domains and are not registered in tests/corpus/assets/manifest.json (assetRefs is empty) — the browser's img-src CSP blocks any remote fetch regardless of interceptor/manifest registration, so no stored fixture is required for this pair's blocked/partial assertions; do not permit live DNS/HTTP traffic.

Current production preview CSP blocks remote Native images. Record card-text rendering and image blocking separately; intercepting a request does not bypass CSP. Do not claim fully rendered images if naturalWidth remains zero.
Inspect intended click target without following it.

crosscheck.js's unsafeNativeScheme (crosscheck.js:873-879) restricts img.url to http(s) only, exactly like link.url; a data: image URI would CRIT as native_unsafe_scheme there even though it cannot execute script as an src. This pair therefore uses remote https URLs (blocked by the preview CSP, not a defect) rather than data: images, so its crosscheck signal stays about asset richness only; see native-x-structured-bid-object for the data:-image full-render proof.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.
